summary: A satirical news-style essay on the rise of virtual economies, tracing a series of dated events from the launch of the first immaterial stock exchange in September 2023 to the Social Virtuality Initiative in September 2025. It mixes absurd episodes such as a one-pixel art sale, a crashed virtual real estate deal and a virtual bank heist with commentary on regulation, labor and monetary policy. It concludes that economies are ultimately about people and that digital prosperity risks widening real-world poverty.
one_line: Satirical essay on virtual economies, from a virtual stock exchange and BitLeaf to regulation, new jobs and the digital divide.
key_facts: Virtualia Inc. launched the first wholly immaterial stock exchange on September 5, 2023.
On November 12, 2023, digital landscaper Jane Dough bought groceries with BitLeaf, a cryptocurrency backed by the speculative value of digital trees in online worlds.
On March 14, 2024, a single pixelated orange pixel by artist Pixel Van Gogh sold for the equivalent of a small island nation's GDP; the artist called it a critique of economic fragility.
Investor Jack Potts wagered half his fortune on a virtual beachfront property on December 20, 2023.

The platform hosting Jack Potts's property crashed in an unprecedented cyber-attack on February 18, 2024, leaving him with 'nothing but pixels in oblivion'; he said 'It's all part of the game! You win some, you lose some.'
The 'In-Game Regulators Summit' was held on January 22, 2025 in a virtual reality conference room, where proposals for virtual taxes led to virtual riots and a new wave of virtual anarchists.

Michael Workaday, a financial analyst turned professional quest-giver in VRMMORPGs, shared his insights on April 15, 2025; he designs quests for adventurers seeking ingame gold and leads a team of digital blacksmiths.
On July 8, 2025, a virtual bank heist stole innumerable coins that held perceived value higher than the currencies of several developing countries combined.
Governments and central banks are struggling to integrate virtual earnings into GDP and to apply monetary policy to a resource that can be duplicated at will.
The Social Virtuality Initiative was launched on September 16, 2025 with a manifesto championing 'an economy for all'.
The Social Virtuality Initiative's launch event was hosted exclusively online, excluding people without digital literacy and undercutting its aim of bridging the digital divide.
The essay concludes that economies are about people, not avatars, usernames or pixels, and urges balancing innovation with inclusivity.
